help.title: Guide
help.subtitle: How to use Media Audio Lib: where each feature lives and how to run it.

import.title: Adding tracks and folders
import.where: top bar of the Library, or by dropping onto the window.
steps: Press "Add tracks" to pick one or more audio files.
Press "Add folder" to import all the music inside a folder, subfolders included.
You can also drop files or folders straight onto the window.
A summary then lists what was added, what was already there and what could not be imported. A clean import dismisses itself.
Files stay where they are: the library only keeps the list.

organize.title: Searching and sorting
organize.where: top bar and column headers, in the list view.
steps: Type in the search box to filter by title, artist, album, genre or path.
Click a column header to sort the tracks.
Clicking the same column again reverses the order.
Tracks missing that field always sink to the bottom.

views.title: Switching view
views.where: the two icons on the right of the Library bar.
steps: The list icon shows the table with every column.
The grid icon shows the cover previews.
The chosen view is remembered next time you open the app.

metadata.title: Editing metadata
metadata.where: pencil icon on the track row or card.
steps: Open the editor with the pencil icon.
Edit name, artist, album, year and genre; the genre can be picked or typed.
Use "Choose image…" to replace the cover (PNG or JPEG, up to 5 MB).
Press "Save": the changes are written into the file tags, not just the library.
Leaving a field empty removes that value from the file.

player.title: Playing a track
player.where: double click a row or a card; the player appears at the bottom.
steps: Double click the track you want to hear.
The player shows up at the bottom with cover, title and artist.
The arrow expands it to full page; Esc or the down arrow returns to the bar.
The X closes the player.

settings.title: Personalising the app
settings.where: gear icon in the top right corner.
steps: Under the "General" tab choose language, text size and light or dark theme.
The "System" theme follows the Windows setting.
Every choice applies straight away and is remembered.
